## Company overview

Freedom Holdings Corp. (FRHC) is a Financial Conglomerates company in the Financial Services sector, with a market capitalization of $10.82B. Through its subsidiaries it provides securities brokerage, securities dealing, market making, investment research, investment counseling, retail and commercial banking, and insurance products. It reports four segments: Brokerage, Banking, Insurance, and Other.

The Brokerage segment covers investment banking services such as M&A, underwriting and capital markets advisory, margin lending collateralized by securities and cash in the customer's account, capital raising solutions, and debt capital markets solutions. The shares trade on NasdaqCM at 169.65, within a 52-week range of 107.97-178.00.

## Financial commentary

Revenue rose from $795.69M in fiscal 2023 to $1.64B in 2024, $1.99B in 2025 and $2.17B in 2026. Growth has therefore been rapid overall, though the increases have been smaller in the most recent years. The latest reported revenue growth figure is 27.8%.

Net income has been much more volatile than revenue. It was $205.14M in 2023, rose to $379.11M in 2024, fell to $76.29M in 2025 and recovered to $153.33M in 2026. The net margin is 8.4% and return on equity is 10.7%. Debt/Equity is 1.82, and EV/Revenue is 5.3. The company pays no dividend, with a yield of 0.0%.

## Comps commentary

The comparison group is Interactive Brokers, Charles Schwab, Robinhood, Stifel Financial and Virtu Financial, with price-to-book as the primary multiple. FRHC trades at a P/B of 6.8 against a peer median of 3.8, a premium of 78%. On earnings, its trailing P/E of 67.3 compares with a median of 17.6 (+282%), and its forward P/E of 37.7 compares with 12.2 (+209%).

The premium comes with weaker profitability. FRHC's ROE of 10.7% is 55% below the peer median of 23.6%. Revenue growth of 27.8% is 6% above the median of 26.3%, so the growth advantage is slight. Its dividend yield of 0.0% compares with a median of 1.3%. Overall, the market is pricing FRHC well above its peers on most valuation measures, while returns on equity trail them.
